messages:
maria-ops: FYI I started seeing a card-level degradation signal in gpool-west-2. Node gpu-112/card3 has ~430 correctable ECCs over 3h and a rising slope. No Xid crashes yet but IO latency for that pod jumped.
kevin-infra: can you paste the raw metric? want to check smoothing and burstiness before deciding a hardware action. :eyes:
repair-bot: automated-alert: gpu_card_correctable{node=\"gpu-112\",card=\"3\"} rate=0.038/s over 15m, total=430 (3h).
prasanna-sre: if it's steady it's usually noise; if it's stair-steppy we prefer schedule replacement. What's the per-card SNR and retry rate?
lina-mlinfra: digging through traces — KV cache misses spike aligns with the correctable bursts when seq_len > 1024. Could be heat/PCI retries under long sequences.
adam-enginfra: ops context: west-2 has tight spare capacity this week (reserved runs), replacing a card will need rolling-migration scheduling, might push jobs to other zones. So prefer a soft-evict if possible.
maria-ops: here's the quick PromQL I ran: 
```\nsum by(card) (increase(gpu_ecc_correctable_total{pool=~\"gpool-west.*\"}[3h]))\n```
card=3 shows the outlier.
kevin-infra: agree run more signal fusion before replacement. Proposal: combine three signals into an index (correctable-rate, retry-count, pci-error-rate) with a hysteresis window (1h EWMA + 3h raw). Trigger actionable when index > 0.7 for 2 windows. That avoids flapping.
prasanna-sre: +1. Also add Xid spikes and process-level OOMs as veto signals so we don't evict healthy cards during unrelated infra failures.
lina-mlinfra: I'll instrument an extra metric for sequence-length-correlated retries so we can separate workload-induced noise.
adam-enginfra: policy question: when index crosses threshold, do we do soft-evict (drain >= 5m, try reschedule) or immediate replacement? Cost/availability tradeoffs.
maria-ops: suggested playbook draft: 1) validate index over 2 windows 2) run a controlled soft-evict (5–10m drain) to see if error stops 3a) if errors stop — mark device for monitoring, schedule replace in weekly maintenance 3b) if errors persist — schedule rolling replace (one card) with cooldown 24h 4) if multiple cards in a node show correlated errors — consider whole-node retire.
repair-bot: note: soft-evict will preempt low-priority batch jobs per current scheduler config.
kevin-infra: for the rolling replace job we should add a simulated dry-run step to measure cross-region failover cost: estimate tokens lost / SLA risk if we shift 10% of load to east-1.
prasanna-sre: propose adding a quick mitigation: kernel-level ECC patience increase (tunables) for 6h to see if retries converge. That buys time for a scheduled replace rather than emergency.
lina-mlinfra: thermal logs on gpu-112 show 5C above pool median during heavy seqs. Could be cooling or a driver regression. Recommend we run a driver rollback test on a mirrored node before replacement.
adam-enginfra: approved: run the fusion-index experiment and the soft-evict test on gpu-112 (dry-run only, no immediate hardware RMA). Maria, pls schedule the soft-evict window during 02:00–04:00 UTC to minimize batch disruptions.
maria-ops: scheduled soft-evict at 02:30 UTC, I will post results. Also opening a replacement ticket if index stays high after 24h: RMA-INVEST-1987.
kevin-infra: we should also document the cost calc in the ticket: replacement vs requeue cost + risk. I'll add an estimated $/card and estimated job delay minutes.
prasanna-sre: if the soft-evict causes <1% task failures and restarts, we accept and schedule replacement in maintenance window. If >=1% then escalate to manual rollback + immediate replace.
adam-enginfra: final ask — can someone add a one-pager for oncall that summarizes the fusion-index and the three-tier response? Keep it to max 6 bullets. Lina?
lina-mlinfra: will draft and link into the playbooks doc.
maria-ops: results: soft-evict executed, correctable-rate dropped to background for 40m then resumed. Index still >0.7 after 12h. We will proceed with rolling replace of card3 during weekly maintenance. Not an emergency.
kevin-infra: thanks — let's also tag this node for extra observability and keep the thermal/driver tickets open.
prasanna-sre: closing the loop: add a note to the incident log with thresholds used and the timeline. Good runbook refinement. :thumbsup:
repair-bot: ticket RMA-INVEST-1987 updated: status=scheduled, replace_window=weekly-maint-3, observer=adam-enginfra.
